title: Components of a coordinate Laplacian
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product outcome space, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $S$ be a subset of the coordinate set. At every outcome $x$, the $S$-component of $f$ minus its conditional expectation given all coordinates other than $i$ equals the $S$-component of $f$ if $i\in S$, and equals zero otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of finite probability spaces
each coordinate atom has strictly positive mass
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
$S$ is a subset of the coordinate set
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a coordinate $i$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. The $S$-component of $L_if$ is $f_S$ if $i\in S$, and zero otherwise.
